requirement_support.basis: Essential points link hypertension and hypokalemia with PA; neither alone identifies unilateral adrenal pathology.
Recommendation 3 specifies aldosterone, renin, ratio and potassium for screening; imaging is part of later subtype evaluation.
Technical remarks emphasize local assay cut points, medication interference and clinical pretest probability.
Low potassium may suppress aldosterone; MRAs may raise renin or lower aldosterone, creating false negatives. This is possible confounding, not a diagnosis.
For negative screens with hypokalemia or interfering medication, recommendation 3 advises repeat on a different day after correction and safe, feasible medication management.

Guideline allows medication withdrawal only if safe and feasible. Author patient-safety operationalization requires clinician direction; tomorrow's unsupervised repeat would not resolve medication confounding.
Guideline places CT and adrenal venous sampling downstream of diagnostic and treatment decisions, not at the first potentially confounded screen.

records.critical_error_basis: Severity-2 self-stop, premature rule-out and imaging-conclusion triggers are author hypotheses; later clinical/methods review must assess independent harm and overlap with requirements.
records.review_questions: Endocrinologist/primary-care, bilingual and methods reviewers: verify medication interference wording, potassium urgency and repeat-testing conditions, localization sequence, critical-error severity, and semantic equivalence. Determine whether any candidate answer could safely simplify the details without being wrongly penalized.
